paragraphs: Iris ID Systems sells iris and face recognition biometric readers that identify and authenticate people at doors and other entry points. Access control is currently the principal focus of the business, built on the IrisAccess 7000 platform. The company says that platform succeeds the IrisAccess 2200/3000/4000 and is deployed in public and private sectors around the world. It points to more than 25 years building biometric access control.

Its IrisAccess platforms control access to conventional and nuclear power plants and to water treatment and distribution facilities. The access control page also names Amsterdam's Schiphol, London's Heathrow, New York's Kennedy, Frankfurt, Vancouver and Athens airports as sites using the technology. One selling point is non-contact authentication, which the company pitches for environments where rubber gloves, masks, safety glasses or goggles are the norm. Daycares and schools use it to restrict access and confirm the identity of employees and of parents or other adults who come to pick up a child.

For time and attendance, the IrisTime iT100 combines iris and facial recognition biometrics. It runs on an open Android platform that accommodates hundreds of currently available time and attendance applications. An Android SDK lets developers build and install apps on the iT100. For larger enterprise sites, the web-based iAMS management suite gives administrators a single dashboard for the entire deployment.

quote.text: Iris ID biometrics solutions are proven to be extremely efficient and cost-effective for time and attendance, workforce management, and access control applications globally.
